index.hero.title: Summit 2026
index.p1:
(非正式翻譯版本僅作佔位) g0v Summit 2026 focuses on civic tech and public-private collaboration. This year, after community discussions, we set the theme as “Invite Yourself,” reflecting on fragmented public spaces and fading momentum. We hope to broaden participation and actively connect civic groups across Taiwan, rekindling constructive contributions through diverse session formats in the spirit of open collaboration.
We look forward to presenting civic tech and advocacy practices, showing the potential of civic action across fields. Whether sharing inspiring wins or lessons from failures, we invite civic hackers and on-the-ground advocates to gather, understand each other, and encourage newcomers to take ownership—turning the Summit into a place that stitches together actors in civil society.

index.p3:
(非正式翻譯版本僅作佔位) g0v is a civic tech community born in Taiwan. By offering more readable information and more usable digital services, it advances civic engagement in public issues. In g0v’s polycentric universe, projects self-organize and contribute autonomously, practicing open collaboration at the grassroots level and releasing results under open-source licenses so more people can build on them.
Through hackathons and hands-on projects, and to connect practitioners of civic tech, open data, and digital governance in Taiwan and worldwide, the g0v community holds “g0v Summit” every two years—bringing civic hackers, NGOs, public servants, and advocates together to share stories and experiences.
index.p4:
g0v (gov-zero) is a grassroots social movement community dedicated to deepening the civic engagements and connections between the social arena and citizens. You can find like-minded partners in the g0v community, put your ideas into practice in a grassroots manner, and then release the results under an open-source license, letting people stand on your shoulders.
g0v replaces the “o” in gov with “0”, thereby reimagining the role of government from scratch, and represents the vision from 0 to 1 of the generation of digital natives.

guidelines.p1: g0v Summit 2026 accepts proposals via the official Google Form only. Submissions close at 23:59 (UTC+8) on Jan 15, 2026. You may edit your submission in the form until the deadline. After review, accepted proposals will be confirmed with submitters. Once confirmed, privacy-related info (except nickname) will be removed, and the agenda will start to be published in late March.
guidelines.t2: CFP theme — mapping civic coordinates from nodes to networks
guidelines.p2:
Someone told us, “Once bitten by a snake, you’ll fear the rope for ten years.” Taiwan’s civil society is facing challenges and shocks, yet we refuse to stay fearful. We pick up the “rope” and turn fear into action—phah—crafting a resilient 3D coordinate system of values, actions, and spaces.
In this coming summit, every participant is a “point” in this 3D space—this is phah-kat. No one is an outsider; everyone can locate themselves by values, actions, and space:
guidelines.axes.x: X axis (values): radical transparency/open vs. autonomy/privacy
guidelines.axes.y: Y axis (actions): growing upward vs. rooting downward
guidelines.axes.z: Z axis (space): in-system government vs. grassroots civic sphere
guidelines.p3: When we cast out the rope and talk with others, points connect into lines—even opposing lines can be woven together. Countless lines then form a mesh. On this community-woven web, isolated nodes become clusters; single-thread dialogues evolve into collaborative ecosystems. It is both a safety net and a launchpad for civic creativity—a plural, open space where everyone can find their place.

guidelines.faq.q1: 1. When will results be announced? Will both accepted and declined be notified?
guidelines.faq.a1: We will email both accepted and declined submitters by end of February, and publish the confirmed agenda in late March.
guidelines.faq.q2: 2. Can I edit my submission after sending?
guidelines.faq.a2: Yes. Until the Jan 31 form deadline, you can revisit with the same account and edit your submission.
guidelines.faq.q3: 3. Can one person join multiple proposals?
guidelines.faq.a3: Yes. The committee will consider speaker diversity, content, and other factors holistically.
guidelines.faq.q4: 4. I have special concerns and don’t want recording/streaming. Should I submit?
guidelines.faq.a4: Yes. The submission form includes a field to note this preference.
guidelines.faq.q5: 1. My session is not in Mandarin. Will translation be provided?
guidelines.faq.a5: All rooms provide AI live transcription (Mandarin→English, English→Mandarin).
guidelines.faq.q6: 2. I need special assistance (e.g., sign language, accessibility). Can the event help?
guidelines.faq.a6: Please note needs in your submission. Within venue and budget limits, we’ll do our best to assist.
guidelines.faq.a7: Basic AV (projector, mics, streaming), shared notes, sli.do for Q&A, and 110V power outlets throughout. Note special needs in your submission.
guidelines.faq.q8: 1. I’m not in Taipei—will lodging/transport be arranged or subsidized?
guidelines.faq.a8: Sorry, we do not provide lodging or transport support.
guidelines.faq.q9: 2. I’m a foreign participant—can the event help with visa/entry documents?
guidelines.faq.a9: We will provide an invitation letter upon acceptance for visa and entry. For other visa questions, please see the Bureau of Consular Affairs and contact your local Taiwan mission. If you need any document from us, email programming@summit.g0v.tw.
